summary.intent: Run the GSD manager command center for the CipherBox v1.1 milestone to discuss, plan, and execute three remaining gap-closure phases (42: API unpin integrity, 43: FUSE write durability, 44: IPNS conflict handling) from a UAT audit, with auto-advance chaining across all three.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 was fully completed: all 8 plans executed across 3 waves in isolated worktrees, code reviewed, live-DB schema verified, and marked complete in ROADMAP/STATE. Phase 43's branch was rebased onto the completed phase-42 branch and planning was initiated (research agent spawned, validation doc written). Phase 44 had its context and discussion log committed but planning had not yet started.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) was protected only by JwtAuthGuard with no CID ownership check — any account holder could destroy another user's pinned content; signup is open (Web3Auth), making this a wide cross-tenant data-destruction surface

Kubo v0.40 runs with the 'server' profile which disables only local-network discovery but keeps full public DHT participation, meaning every pinned CID's provider record is broadcast to DHT crawlers — CIDs are public identifiers by design

Writable-share saves drop prunedCids without unpinning (shared-write.ts:450) — there is no legitimate cross-user unpin path; the only paths to the no-row case are double-delete races, compensation retries, and malicious calls

BYO (bring-your-own IPFS) unpin was broken in both directions before Phase 42: the server-side advisory row delete path never called provider.unpin, and the BYO provider stub silently swallowed the call

pnpm/jest invocation gotcha: `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api test -- --testPathPattern=X` BREAKS because pnpm's argument terminator causes jest to treat the pattern as a positional regex; correct form is `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api exec jest --testPathPattern='X'`

1Password SSH commit signing requires dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true on all git commit tool calls; signing failures ('agent returned an error / fatal: failed to write commit object') require restarting the 1Password desktop app before retrying

gsd commit helper returns 'committed: false' as a false negative in some cases — commits may have actually landed; always verify with `git log --oneline -1` rather than trusting the helper return value

No .prettierignore existed in the repo, causing prettier to mangle planning docs and break VALIDATION.md table cells (pipe chars interpreted as table column separators); created .prettierignore covering .planning/, .claude/agents/gsd-*.md, .claude/commands/gsd/, .claude/gsd-core/, and related GSD-managed paths

The IPNS write-auth model is purely cryptographic — IPNS records are signed by the key holder, so any caller with a valid JWT can overwrite another user's IPNS record only if they possess the private key; the server holds all keys, making the threat model different from the unpin case

Postgres advisory xact lock on hashtext(cid) is the correct mechanism to close the concurrent-unpin refcount race; without it, two simultaneous unpin transactions both see the other's row as committed and both skip the outbox insert, leaving a stranded Kubo pin

code.finding: Kubo service uses 'server' profile with swarm port 4001 exposed publicly (tcp+udp); server profile disables LAN discovery only, leaving full DHT participation active — all pinned CIDs become publicly discoverable via DHT crawlers

Unpin errors are silently swallowed with .catch(logger.warn) — callers never read the HTTP response status, which informed the API contract decision to return opaque {success:true} for all outcomes including cross-user attempts

guardedUnpin added in Phase 42: acquires pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)), deletes pinned_cids row, refcounts in-transaction, conditionally inserts pending_unpins outbox row, increments unpinCrossUserAttempts metric on no-row cross-user detection, then calls Kubo pin/rm post-commit best-effort

Upload compensation path called ipfsProvider.unpinFile directly before Phase 42 fix; rerouted through guardedUnpin with a D-13 race-window comment explaining why the cross-user audit metric may fire spuriously on compensation retries

workflow: GSD worktree cleanup helper (cleanup-wave --manifest) is not idempotent: if a previous run partially merged some entries, a rerun on the same manifest reports 'branch_mismatch' for already-merged entries and aborts the whole run; mitigation is to write a reduced manifest containing only the remaining unmerged entries
cleanup-wave cwd bug: the helper resolves repoRoot from cwd, so running it from inside an agent worktree causes false 'base_mismatch' errors for all entries; must always be run from the repo root
Worktree executor subagents frequently leave node_modules and .husky/_ untracked dirs that block git clean during merge; explicitly rm these before running cleanup-wave

openapi.json drifts as a side-effect of `nest build` during compilation gates even when the API contract is unchanged (formatting-only diff of 500+ lines); restore with git checkout -- before the worktree merge to avoid a spurious merge conflict
GSD decision coverage gate uses mechanical grep for literal 'D-07:' citation strings — plan must_haves sections need verbatim decision IDs, not paraphrased references, or the gate fails
Never run full monorepo test suites in gates or subagents due to RAM constraints; always use targeted --testPathPattern or --testNamePattern filters against specific packages
Phase branch rebasing workflow: after closing a phase, rebase the next phase's context-only commits onto the completed branch before planning begins so the planner sees the full merged implementation

friction: gsd-planner socket error mid-execution after writing plans 42-01 through 42-03 required detecting partial completion from filesystem state and spawning a continuation planner for plans 04-08

1Password SSH signing failures ('fatal: failed to write commit object') occurred multiple times throughout the session, requiring user to restart the 1Password desktop app; every git commit call needed dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true
gsd commit helper false negatives: returned 'committed: false' while the commit had actually landed, causing unnecessary retry attempts and confusion
cleanup-wave not idempotent: partial runs leave the manifest in an inconsistent state requiring manual reduced-manifest workarounds to merge the remaining worktrees

42-05 worktree merge left MERGE_HEAD in an incomplete state (all conflicts auto-resolved but the commit step didn't fire) requiring a manual `git commit --no-edit` to conclude it, followed by manual worktree rm and branch -D
zsh multi-glob rm abort: `rm -rf node_modules apps/*/node_modules` fails entirely if any glob pattern has no matches; must use single explicit paths
pnpm/jest double-dash argument terminator causes --testPathPattern to be treated as a positional regex, silently running all tests instead of the targeted subset

User had to correct communication style: assistant presented a menu of answer choices instead of directly answering 'how would a caller unpin a CID they do not own' — required explicit pushback before the answer was given in plain prose
Two accidental input messages ('touring wyatt web bossy') interrupted the session, each requiring a clarification exchange before resuming
